Two independent studies just confirmed what many executives suspected — but now the numbers are undeniable.

PwC found that 74% of AI's economic gains are flowing to just 20% of organizations. Deloitte surveyed 3,235 executives and landed on the same conclusion from a different direction: only 34% of companies are actually reimagining their business with AI. The other 37%? Layering it on top of workflows that have not fundamentally changed.

The enterprise AI market is splitting into two camps. One group is restructuring how decisions get made, how workflows operate, and how business models function. The other group is adding chatbots and summarization tools to processes designed years ago.

Here is the uncomfortable truth: surface-level AI adoption will not be a differentiator by 2027. The tools are commoditizing fast. Every competitor will have access to the same models at roughly the same cost. The only durable advantage comes from structural change — treating AI as a business architecture decision, not an IT project.

The question for any CEO or CTO this week is simple. Which quintile is your organization in — and what evidence do you have beyond intuition?
